title: Inaccessible cardinals and rank models

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 80; 84–85 (§18, Theorem 18.16; §19, reflection and rank-model boundary); revision 2026-01-31

based_on.title: An Introduction to Set Theory
based_on.pages: 101–102 (Theorems 41–42 and Exercise 34, hereditary-size and rank-stage cardinality and closure bounds); version 2014-11-21

summary: Use regularity and strong-limit bounds to prove that an inaccessible rank stage satisfies every ZFC axiom, including Replacement and Choice.
abstract: A rank stage may contain all subsets of each of its objects while still needing a separate bound on the outputs of a definable function. A strongly inaccessible cardinal is an uncountable cardinal with two bounds: fewer smaller ordinals cannot reach it, and the power set of any smaller cardinal still has size below it. At such a height, every earlier rank stage, and therefore every object in the proposed model, has size below the height. Regularity then bounds the ranks of all outputs indexed by any one of its objects. This supplies Replacement, while explicit rank estimates give the remaining ZF axioms and place ambient well-orders inside the stage to establish Choice. The result is one transitive set model satisfying every ZFC axiom at the supplied inaccessible height. The construction is conditional on that cardinal; finite-family reflection by itself chooses heights separately for the formulas being reflected.
